title: Pika Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Cost per Video
summary: Pika pricing offers plans with monthly credit limits that determine how many videos you can generate. Find the right tier based on your production needs.
body_markdown:
## Pika vs Luma Dream Machine and Krea


Priced per second of finished video, Pika is mid-pack: three times Veo's rate, close to Hailuo's, and well under Runway and Kling. These rates are API prices, so they rank the engines, not the app plans you'd actually buy.


### Entry price and monthly allowance


At $0.013 per second,[Veo is the cheapest](https://varosity.ai/blog/ai-video-api-prices-per-second) , so a 10-second clip costs about $0.13. Pika is at $0.04 per second, or $0.40 for the same clip, **so it's easy to compare against vendors using either pricing model** .


Hailuo is at $0.0417, a difference too small to decide anything, so you need to compare by features and integrations.


At $0.056, Runway costs 1.4 times Pika, and Kling at $0.084 costs about 2.1 times Pika, or $0.84 per 10-second clip. At 100 clips a month, that's $40 on Pika against $84 on Kling.


Neither Luma Dream Machine nor Krea meters its plans in seconds; each uses its own credits. Compare them on one job: the number of clips you need per month, at the length you need, divided into each plan's monthly credits.


Pika's own plans are on[pika.art](https://pika.art/) , and Krea's are on[krea.ai](https://krea.ai/) . Read both against your clip count, checked 17 Nov 2026.


### Free tier and watermark


Treat a free tier as a test budget. Spend it on the exact shot type you'll sell, because failed generations usually consume allowance too.


Check each free tier for a watermark, since a watermarked clip can't go to a client, which makes the free tier a trial only.


### Commercial rights and fit


Check the commercial-use terms on the plan you'd pay for, not the one you tested on, because rights often differ between tiers. If you sell clips to clients, confirm those terms in writing before you commit credits.


When the job fits an alternative better than Pika, the alternative wins. For bulk clips where cost per second is the only constraint, Veo's $0.013 rate was the lowest in the cited comparison, though Google's current video model is Gemini Omni Flash, so check its pricing too.


For work that needs Krea's image tools alongside video, Krea saves you a second subscription.


Pika wins on a middle-of-the-road job, where Runway and Kling cost 1.4 to 2.1 times as much for no gain you need.
